title: Mathematical Methods for Physics
description: Equip physics students with the analytical and computational methods needed for upper-division mechanics, electromagnetism, quantum mechanics, statistical physics, and research-level problem solving.

topics.title: Complex Numbers and Analytic Functions
topics.description: Complex analysis turns oscillation, waves, potentials, and contour integrals into a powerful geometric language for physics.

children.title: Complex algebra and geometry
children.description: Students learn to move fluently between algebraic, polar, exponential, and geometric views of complex quantities.

children.title: Analytic functions
children.description: Analyticity packages differentiability, geometry, and physical constraints into one idea that appears in potentials and wave problems.

children.title: Contour integration
children.description: Contour methods make many real integrals and response calculations tractable.

topics.title: Linear Algebra, Operators, and Hilbert Space Methods
topics.description: Physics uses linear spaces to describe modes, states, observables, and coupled systems. This unit strengthens the linear algebra beneath mechanics and quantum theory.

children.title: Vector spaces and inner products
children.description: Students learn the geometry of state spaces, function spaces, and orthogonality.

children.title: Eigenvalue problems
children.description: Eigenvectors and eigenvalues reveal normal modes, stationary states, and stable directions.

children.title: Function spaces
children.description: Continuous systems require extending finite-dimensional intuition to functions.

topics.title: Vector Calculus and Curvilinear Coordinates
topics.description: Vector calculus is the working language of fields, fluxes, conservation laws, fluids, and electromagnetism.

children.title: Differential operators
children.description: Gradient, divergence, curl, and Laplacian encode local change and conservation.

children.title: Integral theorems
children.description: Integral theorems connect local differential laws to global physical balances.

children.title: Coordinate systems
children.description: Choosing coordinates that match symmetry turns impossible-looking problems into solvable ones.

topics.title: Tensors and Index Notation
topics.description: Tensors give a compact, coordinate-aware language for rotations, stress, inertia, relativity, and anisotropic materials.

children.title: Index notation
children.description: Index notation reduces complicated vector and tensor identities to disciplined symbol manipulation.

children.title: Tensor transformations
children.description: Students learn what it means for a physical quantity to be independent of coordinate description.

children.title: Physical tensors
children.description: The abstract notation becomes concrete through familiar physical objects.

topics.title: Ordinary Differential Equations and Dynamical Systems
topics.description: ODEs model oscillations, circuits, decay, orbits, and stability. This unit makes differential equations feel like physical mechanisms.

children.title: Linear ODE methods
children.description: Students learn the standard solution tools that recur throughout physics.

children.title: Systems and phase space
children.description: System form reveals coupled dynamics and stability.

children.title: Nonlinear dynamics preview
children.description: Many real systems are nonlinear; students need qualitative tools even when closed forms fail.

topics.title: Fourier Series and Orthogonal Expansions
topics.description: Fourier methods decompose physical systems into modes, making waves, heat flow, and boundary-value problems analyzable.

children.title: Fourier series
children.description: Periodic functions become sums of sines and cosines, which often match physical normal modes.

children.title: Sturm-Liouville theory
children.description: This frames many physics eigenfunction expansions as one general theory.

children.title: Applications to boundary problems
children.description: Students learn how boundary conditions choose the allowed modes.

topics.title: Fourier and Laplace Transforms
topics.description: Transforms convert differential equations and convolutions into algebraic problems, especially for waves, signals, response, and initial-value systems.

children.title: Fourier transform
children.description: Students learn frequency-domain thinking for localized and nonperiodic phenomena.

children.title: Laplace transform
children.description: Laplace methods handle initial conditions, forcing, and transients cleanly.

children.title: Spectral interpretation
children.description: Transforms reveal which scales or frequencies dominate a physical process.

topics.title: Special Functions and Orthogonal Polynomials
topics.description: Special functions are the natural solutions of physics in symmetric geometries and separated differential equations.

children.title: Classical special functions
children.description: Students learn the recurring functions that appear in quantum, E&M, heat, and wave problems.

children.title: Generating functions and recurrences
children.description: These tools make special functions calculable and structurally understandable.

children.title: Asymptotic behavior
children.description: Physical interpretation often depends on limits, not exact formulas.

topics.title: Partial Differential Equations
topics.description: PDEs describe fields evolving in space and time. This unit organizes the main equation types and solution strategies.

children.title: Canonical PDEs
children.description: Students learn the signatures of diffusion, wave propagation, and equilibrium fields.

children.title: Separation of variables
children.description: Separation converts many PDEs into eigenvalue problems and mode expansions.

children.title: Classification and characteristics
children.description: Classification helps students choose appropriate methods and understand physical behavior.

topics.title: Green's Functions and Distributions
topics.description: Green's functions turn point-source responses into full solutions and are one of the most powerful methods in theoretical physics.

children.title: Delta functions and distributions
children.description: Students learn a precise language for point sources, impulses, and idealized densities.

children.title: Green's function construction
children.description: The central idea is to solve a problem once for a point source, then assemble general solutions.

children.title: Physical applications
children.description: Students connect Green's functions to electrostatics, waves, quantum propagators, and response theory.

topics.title: Calculus of Variations and Variational Principles
topics.description: Variational thinking unifies mechanics, optics, fields, and approximation methods through the idea of stationary action or energy.

children.title: Euler-Lagrange equations
children.description: Students learn how differential equations emerge from optimizing functionals.

children.title: Constrained variational problems
children.description: Constraints and multipliers model real physical restrictions and conservation laws.

children.title: Physics principles
children.description: This unit connects mathematical variation to the structure of mechanics and fields.

topics.title: Probability, Statistics, and Random Processes in Physics
topics.description: Probability links microscopic uncertainty to macroscopic laws and supports data analysis, statistical mechanics, and noise modeling.

children.title: Probability distributions
children.description: Students learn the distributions that recur in measurement, thermal systems, and stochastic models.

children.title: Random variables and correlations
children.description: Correlation functions reveal structure in fluctuating systems.

children.title: Stochastic processes preview
children.description: Noise-driven dynamics appear in diffusion, Brownian motion, and experimental signals.

topics.title: Approximation, Perturbation, and Asymptotic Methods
topics.description: Exact solutions are rare. Approximation methods teach students to extract reliable physics from small parameters and limiting regimes.

children.title: Perturbation theory
children.description: Students learn systematic correction methods for problems close to solvable ones.

children.title: Asymptotic expansions
children.description: Asymptotics prioritize useful approximations over convergent exactness.

children.title: Dimensional analysis and scaling
children.description: Scaling exposes the governing parameters before calculation begins.

topics.title: Numerical and Computational Methods for Physics
topics.description: World-class mathematical methods should include computation, because many realistic physical systems require numerical exploration.

children.title: Numerical linear algebra
children.description: Students learn computational versions of eigenvalue and linear-system problems.

children.title: Numerical ODE/PDE methods
children.description: This gives practical ways to solve models that lack closed forms.

children.title: Computational validation
children.description: Students learn to treat numerical output as evidence that must be checked.

topics.title: Synthesis Applications Across Physics
topics.description: The final unit makes the methods cohere by revisiting major physics domains and choosing the right mathematical tool for each problem.

children.title: Classical mechanics
children.description: Students connect linear algebra, ODEs, variational methods, and perturbation theory to motion.

children.title: Quantum mechanics
children.description: Students see operators, Hilbert spaces, special functions, and perturbation methods as the grammar of quantum theory.

children.title: Electromagnetism and statistical physics
children.description: Fields and ensembles show how vector calculus, PDEs, Green's functions, probability, and transforms work together.
